---
framework: Systems Thinking
---

# Route consolidation for perishables

The dispatch team redrew the delivery routes eight months ago around a simple rule: never let a refrigerated van carry a partial load past a forty percent fill rate if a nearby stop could top it off within a fifteen minute detour. Fuel cost per delivered unit dropped by a bit more than a fifth, and van count on the road on a typical day fell from eleven to nine without cutting the number of daily deliveries.

The interesting side effect, not the one the change was made for, is that route density is now high enough in the two core neighborhoods that a van passes within a few streets of almost any address in that zone at some point in its run. Nobody set out to build that density, it fell out of solving the fill-rate problem, but it means the marginal cost of adding one more stop to an existing route in those two neighborhoods is now close to the lowest it has ever been, which is not true of the newer, sparser zones the service has been expanding into this year.
